title: Selection sort
description:
Write `void selectionSort(std::vector<int>& values)` that sorts into ascending order.

Selection sort: find the smallest element and swap it into position 0. Then find the smallest of the rest and swap it into position 1. Carry on until the end.

```
[5 3 8 1]   smallest is 1: swap with position 0
[1 3 8 5]   smallest of the rest is 3: already in place
[1 3 8 5]   smallest of the rest is 5: swap with 8
[1 3 5 8]
```
hints: Two loops: the outer one picks the position to fill, the inner one searches the rest for the index of the smallest value.
After the inner loop, swap the smallest into place with `std::swap(values[i], values[smallest]);`. Stop the outer loop one before the end: the last element is then already in place.
lessonTitle: Sorting, Searching, Big-O and Timing Your Code
